verses.text: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"This is a rule the LORD has commanded: Tell the people of Israel to bring you a red young cow with no marks or anything wrong with it, one that has never worn a yoke.
Give it to Eleazar the priest. It must be taken outside the camp and killed in front of him.
Eleazar the priest will take some of its blood on his finger and sprinkle it seven times toward the front of the Tent of Meeting.
Then the cow must be burned while he watches: its skin, its meat, its blood, and its dung must all be burned.
The priest will take cedar wood, hyssop, and red yarn and throw them into the fire where the cow is burning.
After that, the priest must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water. Then he may come back into the camp, but he will be unclean until evening.
The man who burns the cow must also wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.

Then a man who is clean will gather up the cow's ashes and put them in a clean place outside the camp. They will be kept for the community of Israel to use in the water for washing away uncleanness. It is a sin offering.
The man who gathers up the ashes must wash his clothes, and he will be unclean until evening. This is a rule forever, for the people of Israel and for the foreigners living among them.
Anyone who touches a dead body will be unclean for seven days.
He must wash himself with the water on the third day and on the seventh day, and then he will be clean. But if he does not wash himself on the third and seventh days, he will not be clean.

Anyone who touches a dead body and does not wash himself makes the LORD's Holy Tent unclean. That person must be cut off from Israel. Because the cleansing water was not sprinkled on him, he is unclean. His uncleanness stays on him.
This is the teaching for when someone dies in a tent: Anyone who goes into the tent, and anyone who is already in it, will be unclean for seven days.
Every open jar without a lid tied on it will be unclean.
Out in the open fields, anyone who touches someone killed with a sword, or someone who died naturally, or a human bone, or a grave, will be unclean for seven days.
To make the unclean person clean, put some ashes from the burned sin offering into a jar and pour fresh running water over them.

Then a man who is clean must take a hyssop branch, dip it in the water, and sprinkle the tent and everything in it, and the people who were there. He must also sprinkle anyone who has touched a human bone, a person who was killed, someone who died, or a grave.

The clean man must sprinkle the unclean person on the third day and the seventh day. On the seventh day he will make him clean. Then the person being made clean must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and that evening he will be clean.

But anyone who is unclean and does not make himself clean must be cut off from the community, because he has made the LORD's holy place unclean. The cleansing water has not been sprinkled on him, so he is unclean.
This is a rule forever for them. The man who sprinkles the cleansing water must also wash his clothes, and anyone who touches the cleansing water will be unclean until evening.
Anything an unclean person touches becomes unclean, and anyone who touches it will be unclean until evening."
